      "partial_result": "# Critique of Fable consultation 05f2cad4e3ad478f: STOP rank-32 LoRA on PE's upper 6 blocks\n\n## Verdict: conditional GO for a narrow gate\n\nRun a CPU mechanics check, then one 100-update TRAIN pilot, and only if the mechanics pass. I'd fund it because it's cheap and bounded, and not because I expect it to pass. Fable's STOP depends on claims the evidence doesn't support. Its cost argument is fair, but it presents a guessed prior as if it were an established result. If the pilot fails, the conclusion is that this declared procedure failed, not that low-rank learning failed.\n\n## Checking Fable's claims\n\n1. **\"Every measured state improves monotonically\": false as stated.** There are two encoder timepoints (0 and 100), so no trajectory was measured. Large at final encoder/initial head scores 95.6877557 R@1, which is above final/final at 95.6720176. That is non-monotone along the head axis. The counterfactual heads are parameter swaps, not points along training.\n\n2. **\"A rank constraint necessarily slows function-space learning; its only gain route is over-adaptation damage, and none is shown\": not established.**\n   - With \u03b1=r (scale 1), Kaiming A (bound about 1/\u221a768 \u2248 0.036), and Adam on B at lr 1e-4, each \u0394W entry moves roughly 1e-4\u00b70.036\u00b7\u221a32 \u2248 2e-5 per step. The dense tail moves at about 1e-5. The steps differ in geometry; the low-rank step isn't obviously smaller.\n   - Two endpoints can't tell \"learns less\" apart from \"dense updates partly damaged PE's pretrained generality on held products\". Both fit PE starting ahead and ending behind.\n   - Normalizing by headroom confirms PE gained less. Raw R@1 headroom closed is Large 80.3% vs PE 71.8%; raw mAP@R is 56.4% vs 48.7%. That still doesn't identify which mechanism caused it.\n\n3. **The literature claim misreads both papers** (I checked the abstracts).\n   - Hu et al. 2021: \"LoRA performs on-par or better than fine-tuning in model quality on RoBERTa, DeBERTa, GPT-2, and GPT-3.\"\n   - Biderman et al. 2024: LoRA \"substantially underperforms\" full fine-tuning in code/math instruction tuning (~100K pairs) and continued pretraining (20B tokens). It also \"better maintains the base model's performance on tasks outside the target domain\" and \"mitigates forgetting more than \u2026 weight decay and dropout.\"\n   - Neither paper covers 100 updates, 6,400 images, or retrieval on held-out products.
